question.text: Whether the bars listed in RCW 9.96.060(2)(a)-(i) apply to the standalone RCW 9.96.060(6) substance use disorder treatment route.
question.whyItMatters: The answer determines whether a qualifying subsection (6) applicant with a pending charge, domestic-violence history or other subsection (2) bar is excluded from the treatment route.
question.existingEvidenceResult: The existing 2026-08-01 Washington legal review and current track registry expressly preserve this as an unanswered build blocker; the existing adopted route decision identifies subsection (6) but did not resolve subsection (2) applicability.

authorityRead.title: RCW 9.96.060, Vacating records of conviction for misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor offenses

currentTextObserved.subsection2Opening: The subsection (2) bar sentence begins with an express exception for subsections (3), (4), (5), and (6).
currentTextObserved.subsection2Bars: The following subsection (2) bars are then listed in paragraphs (a)-(i): incomplete sentence terms, pending charges, violent offenses, specified DUI/intoxication or prior-offense conditions, specified sex offenses, domestic violence conditions, the ordinary waiting period, a new crime in the prior three years, and protection/no-contact/antiharassment/civil-restraint conditions.
currentTextObserved.subsection6: A person convicted under the enumerated drug statutes who completes a substance use disorder program and files proof, or obtains a qualifying assessment plus six months of substantial compliance and progress documented by written status update, must have the conviction or convictions vacated upon verification.

authorityRead.relevantProvision: RCW 9.96.060(2) expressly says its bar list applies except as provided in subsection (6); subsection (6) then states its own mandatory treatment-route conditions without incorporating the subsection (2) bar list.

authorityRead.title: 2023 sp.s. c. 1, § 11 (2E2SSB 5536), amendment to RCW 9.96.060

currentTextObserved.section11Subsection2: The enacted amendment adds (6) to the parenthetical exceptions in subsection (2).
currentTextObserved.section11Subsection6: The same enacted section adds the standalone treatment-route text and its mandatory vacatur upon verification.

authorityRead.relevantProvision: The session law confirms the textual structure was enacted together: subsection (2) was amended to except subsection (6), and subsection (6) was added as a mandatory route.

determination.supportedInterpretation: For a qualifying RCW 9.96.060(6) treatment-route applicant, the exclusion/bar list in RCW 9.96.060(2)(a)-(i) does not apply. The statute expressly places subsection (6) outside that bar sentence and supplies separate subsection (6) conditions.
determination.confidenceBasis: Direct current statutory text, corroborated by the enacted 2023 special-session amendment that simultaneously inserted the subsection (6) exception into subsection (2) and added the treatment route.

limits: This determination resolves only the applicability of the subsection (2)(a)-(i) bar sentence to subsection (6).

It does not remove subsection (6) requirements: an enumerated conviction, qualifying program completion or qualifying assessment/status path, six months of substantial compliance on the assessment path, and verification/documentation.
It does not decide any separate instrument, local filing practice, fee, source-freshness, participant-fact, packet, independent-review, or production question already recorded for the family.
It does not amend the track registry or widen eligibility in a packet; any product-state change remains a separate Captain-owned integration/adoption action under the existing controls.
